accepted.s: Under Article 292 of the Constitution, Public Debt of the Union comprises borrowings contracted against the:
accepted.x: Article 292 relates to borrowings by the Government of India against the security of the Consolidated Fund of India. Other liabilities are recorded in the Public Account.
accepted.tq: Recall the constitutional article associated with the borrowing authority.
accepted.sec: Centre's liabilities - internal debt, other liabilities, external debt  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with the classification of the Union Government's liabilities?
o: Loans from foreign governments — Internal debt
accepted.x: Small savings and post-office deposits are other liabilities recorded in the Public Account. Market loans are internal debt, while loans from foreign governments are external debt.
accepted.tq: Distinguish internal debt, other liabilities and external debt by identifying the correct category.
accepted.sec: Centre's liabilities - internal debt, other liabilities, external debt  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following is included among the marketable components of the internal debt of the Union Government?
accepted.x: Marketable internal debt includes market loans, Treasury Bills and Cash Management Bills. Provident funds, small savings and post-office deposits are other liabilities.
accepted.tq: Use category-based elimination among closely related government liabilities.
accepted.sec: Centre's liabilities - internal debt, other liabilities, external debt  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the liabilities of the Central Government:
1. G-Secs constitute more than 90% of Central Government debt.
2. Internal debt constitutes 96.7% of public debt.
3. External liabilities constitute 3.3% of the Centre's total liabilities.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct: G-Secs account for over 90% of Central Government debt, internal debt forms 96.7% of public debt, and external liabilities form 3.3% of total Centre liabilities.
accepted.tq: Test several percentages belonging to the same liability classification.
accepted.sec: Centre's liabilities - internal debt, other liabilities, external debt  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The outstanding liabilities of the Central Government in Budget Estimates 2026-27 were estimated at approximately:
accepted.x: The Centre's outstanding liabilities in BE 2026-27 were estimated at ₹2,14,82,050 crore, or 55.6% of GDP.
accepted.tq: Separate the complete figure from truncated or differently scaled numerical distractors.
accepted.sec: Centre's liabilities - internal debt, other liabilities, external debt  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Market borrowings are regarded as the:
o: largest component of external debt only
accepted.x: Market borrowings are the biggest source of capital receipts of the government.
accepted.tq: Identify the dominant source rather than confusing capital receipts with revenue receipts.
accepted.sec: Market borrowings - share in capital receipts; household savings and government borrowing  [APPSC]

accepted.s: In 2026-27, ‘Borrowings and other liabilities’ accounted for approximately how much of every rupee of government receipts?
accepted.x: Borrowings and other liabilities were estimated to account for 24 paise of every rupee in 2026-27 and formed the single largest receipt head.
accepted.tq: Recall the precise share and reject nearby altered percentages.
accepted.sec: Market borrowings - share in capital receipts; household savings and government borrowing  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the 2026-27 gross and net market borrowings through dated securities?
o: Gross ₹11.73 lakh crore; net ₹17.20 lakh crore
Gross ₹19.03 lakh crore; net ₹6.65 lakh crore
Gross ₹17.20 lakh crore; net ₹11.73 lakh crore
Gross ₹16.96 lakh crore; net ₹17.20 lakh crore
accepted.x: Gross market borrowing through dated securities was ₹17.20 lakh crore and net market borrowing was ₹11.73 lakh crore in 2026-27.
accepted.tq: Watch for reversal of gross and net figures.
accepted.sec: Market borrowings - share in capital receipts; household savings and government borrowing  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding market borrowing in 2026-27:
1. The weighted average maturity was 19.03 years.
2. The weighted average yield was 6.65%.
3. Switches and buybacks were undertaken to ease redemption pressures.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The weighted average maturity was 19.03 years, the yield was 6.65%, and switches and buybacks were used to ease redemptions.
accepted.tq: Combine two numerical facts with the associated debt-management measure.
accepted.sec: Market borrowings - share in capital receipts; household savings and government borrowing  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The total borrowing requirement of the Union Government for 2026-27 was estimated at:
accepted.x: The total borrowing requirement for 2026-27 was estimated at ₹16,95,768 crore.
accepted.tq: Distinguish total borrowing requirement from gross and net market borrowing.
accepted.sec: Market borrowings - share in capital receipts; household savings and government borrowing  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Household financial savings contribute to government borrowing through which of the following channels?
1. Bank deposits reflected through SLR holdings
2. Small savings and the National Small Savings Fund
3. Insurance and provident funds
4. Only direct purchase of foreign sovereign bonds
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Household savings flow to government borrowing through bank deposits, small savings/NSSF, and insurance and provident funds. Direct purchase of foreign sovereign bonds is not the stated channel.
accepted.tq: Find the single over-exclusive or unrelated channel among several genuine domestic channels.
accepted.sec: Market borrowings - share in capital receipts; household savings and government borrowing  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding State borrowing:
1. A State owing any amount to the Centre requires the Centre's consent to borrow further.
2. Since 2005-06, external loans to States have been routed through the Centre.
3. For general category States, such external loans are provided on a back-to-back basis.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct under the stated framework for State borrowing and external loans.
accepted.tq: Test the constitutional consent rule together with the post-2005-06 borrowing arrangement.
accepted.sec: State borrowing - net borrowing ceiling, highest debt-GSDP States, AP liabilities  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The net borrowing ceiling for States for 2021-22, as recommended by the Fifteenth Finance Commission, was:
accepted.x: The net borrowing ceiling for States for 2021-22 was 4% of GSDP under the Fifteenth Finance Commission framework.
accepted.tq: Recall the year-specific ceiling and avoid substituting the general fiscal-deficit limit.
accepted.sec: State borrowing - net borrowing ceiling, highest debt-GSDP States, AP liabilities  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Sixteenth Finance Commission has capped the fiscal deficit of States at what percentage of GSDP for 2026-31?
accepted.x: The fiscal deficit of States has been capped at 3% of GSDP for 2026-31 under the Sixteenth Finance Commission framework.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the 2021-22 borrowing ceiling and the 2026-31 fiscal-deficit cap.
accepted.sec: State borrowing - net borrowing ceiling, highest debt-GSDP States, AP liabilities  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which State had the highest debt or outstanding liabilities as a percentage of GSDP among the following in 2023-24?
accepted.x: Punjab had the highest ratio among the listed States at 42.9% of GSDP in 2023-24, followed by West Bengal at 38.3%, Rajasthan at 37.9% and Andhra Pradesh at 34.6%.
accepted.tq: Compare the values in a ranking table and identify the maximum.
accepted.sec: State borrowing - net borrowing ceiling, highest debt-GSDP States, AP liabilities  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following States in descending order of debt or outstanding liabilities as a percentage of GSDP for 2023-24:
A. Rajasthan
B. Andhra Pradesh
C. Punjab
D. West Bengal
accepted.x: The correct descending order is Punjab (42.9%), West Bengal (38.3%), Rajasthan (37.9%) and Andhra Pradesh (34.6%).
accepted.tq: Rank the figures from highest to lowest before checking the sequence options.
accepted.sec: State borrowing - net borrowing ceiling, highest debt-GSDP States, AP liabilities  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes Andhra Pradesh's debt position in 2025-26 revised estimates?
o: Total debt ₹5,68,623 crore and 35.73% of GSDP
Total debt ₹7,11,094 crore and 36.04% of GSDP
Total debt ₹5,64,488 crore and 35.15% of GSDP
Total debt ₹6,35,177 crore and 36.04% of GSDP
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh's total debt in 2025-26 RE was ₹6,35,177 crore, equivalent to 36.04% of GSDP. The other figures refer to different estimates or years.
accepted.tq: Match the amount with the correct year and estimate category.
accepted.sec: State borrowing - net borrowing ceiling, highest debt-GSDP States, AP liabilities  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding Andhra Pradesh's debt is NOT correct?
o: Market borrowing accounted for only 12% of Andhra Pradesh's debt in 2023-24 revised estimates.
Interest payments were ₹37,233 crore in 2025-26 revised estimates.
Market borrowing was ₹4,83,093 crore in 2025-26 revised estimates.
Market borrowing is the largest component of the State's debt.
accepted.x: Market borrowing accounted for 75% of Andhra Pradesh's debt in 2023-24 RE, not 12%. The 12% share related to other liabilities in the composition table.
accepted.tq: Locate the reversed share in a composition table; the largest component is the key check.
accepted.sec: State borrowing - net borrowing ceiling, highest debt-GSDP States, AP liabilities  [APPSC]

accepted.s: According to the 2023-24 revised estimates, the correct descending order of components of Andhra Pradesh's debt is:
o: Market loans > central loans ≈ provident funds > others > small savings
Others > market loans > provident funds > central loans > small savings
Small savings > provident funds > central loans > others > market loans
Market loans > others > central loans ≈ provident funds > small savings
accepted.x: The composition was market loans 75%, others 12%, central loans 6% approximately equal to provident funds 6%, and small savings 1%.
accepted.tq: Arrange components by percentage and preserve the approximate tie.
accepted.sec: State borrowing - net borrowing ceiling, highest debt-GSDP States, AP liabilities  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly states Andhra Pradesh's Budget Estimate for outstanding liabilities in 2026-27?
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh's BE 2026-27 projected outstanding liabilities at ₹7,11,094 crore, approximately 36% of GSDP.
accepted.tq: Separate the latest budget estimate from revised-estimate figures of earlier years.
accepted.sec: State borrowing - net borrowing ceiling, highest debt-GSDP States, AP liabilities  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements regarding State finances is correct?
1. States borrowed ₹5.23 trillion up to October 2025.
2. This represented 62% of the FY26 borrowing plan.
3. The combined fiscal deficit of States was 3.2% of GDP in FY25.
4. Eighteen States recorded fiscal deficits above 3% in FY24.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: All four statements are correct: States borrowed ₹5.23 trillion by October 2025, equal to 62% of the FY26 plan; the combined FY25 deficit was 3.2% of GDP; and 18 States exceeded 3% in FY24.
accepted.tq: Check each time-bound fiscal statistic separately before selecting the coded combination.
accepted.sec: State borrowing - net borrowing ceiling, highest debt-GSDP States, AP liabilities  [APPSC]

accepted.s: India's external debt at the end of December 2024 was estimated at:
o: USD 635.177 billion, equivalent to 36.04% of GDP
USD 711.82 billion, equivalent to 18.4% of GDP
USD 718.2 billion, equivalent to 20.4% of GDP
USD 718.2 billion, equivalent to 18.4% of GDP
accepted.x: India's external debt stood at USD 718.2 billion at end-December 2024, equivalent to 18.4% of GDP in the cited estimate.
accepted.tq: Keep the external-debt amount and its GDP ratio together while rejecting figures from other debt categories.
accepted.sec: External debt - composition, sovereign share, currency, publisher  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about India's external debt:
1. Its external debt-to-GDP ratio was reported as 20.4% in the RBI-based estimate.
2. Foreign exchange reserves covered 90% of external debt.
3. India ranked 21st in the world and 11th among G20 countries.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct for the cited RBI and Economic Survey-based indicators.
accepted.tq: Combine ratio, reserve-cover and ranking data without confusing alternative estimates.
accepted.sec: External debt - composition, sovereign share, currency, publisher  [other exams]

accepted.s: Historically, the largest component of India's external debt has been:
accepted.x: Commercial borrowings have historically been the largest component of India's external debt.
accepted.tq: Identify the principal historical component while excluding domestic-liability categories.
accepted.sec: External debt - composition, sovereign share, currency, publisher  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with India's sovereign external borrowing?
o: Primarily multilateral, concessional and project-linked — ADB is the largest multilateral lender
Primarily commercial and non-concessional — ADB is excluded
Primarily domestic and short-term — NDB is the sole lender
Primarily denominated in domestic currency — AIIB is the only lender
accepted.x: Sovereign external borrowing is mostly multilateral, concessional and project-linked. The ADB is the largest multilateral lender, with a 32.8% share, followed by institutions including the World Bank, NDB and AIIB.
accepted.tq: Match the borrowing character with the correct multilateral lender and avoid absolute distractors.
accepted.sec: External debt - composition, sovereign share, currency, publisher  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which institution publishes ‘India's External Debt: A Status Report’?
o: Department of Economic Affairs, Ministry of Finance
accepted.x: The report is published by the Department of Economic Affairs under the Ministry of Finance. The RBI compiles the quarterly external-debt data.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the institution that publishes the report from the institution that compiles quarterly data.
accepted.sec: External debt - composition, sovereign share, currency, publisher  [other exams]
